briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Tax Fight Turns Political as Rescheduling and Psilocybin Data Light Up the Map
briefs.top: Michigan operators are turning frustration over the 24% wholesale tax into leverage, with the GOP gubernatorial nominee now courting the industry's vote while new stores keep opening in Ann Arbor and Detroit. Nationally, Schedule III momentum and blockbuster psilocybin trial data are pulling capital and optimism back into plant-medicine markets.

local.text: GOP nominee courts cannabis industry with tax-cut pledge — MiCIA endorsed John James after he vowed to repeal the 24% wholesale tax and slash the excise rate from 10% to 5%, giving operators a real electoral path to relief this November.
Michigan sold more weed than ever in 2025 — Retailers moved more product than any year since adult-use launch, proof demand keeps climbing even as the new wholesale tax squeezes margins.

Ann Arbor and Detroit keep adding storefronts — New Standard's Ann Arbor location and C3 Industries' High Profile Cannabis Detroit debut show operators are still betting on Southeast Michigan expansion.

Wholesale-tax trial date locked in for this fall — MiCIA's original constitutional challenge heads to trial in September even as a second lawsuit and a bipartisan repeal bill keep the pressure on Lansing.
Menominee could add four new dispensary licenses — A petition drive would raise the city's cap from nine stores to 13, opening fresh retail slots for operators eyeing the U.P.

national.text: Schedule III process clears another procedural checkpoint — DEA's rescheduling review advanced in August with an NPRM expected before year-end, a shift that would gut 280E and cut effective tax rates from 60% toward the mid-20s for operators.

Compass Pathways' psilocybin holds up at six months — COMP360 showed durable, clinically meaningful response in a second Phase 3 trial, keeping the company on track for an early-2027 commercial launch.

Rescheduling is fueling a fresh M&A wave — Tilray's acquisition of the UK's Lyphe Group and Organigram's closed buyout of Germany's Sanity Group show North American operators racing into medical markets post-Schedule III.

Teen cannabis use hits a record low, CDC data shows — The 2025 Youth Risk Behavior Survey found high-schooler use at its lowest point since tracking began, undercutting a favorite argument against legalization.

Hemp businesses get a short runway on the looming ban — Congress granted a one-month reprieve on the intoxicating-hemp crackdown, buying operators time to adjust even as they push for clearer permanent rules.
